apple.region_label: Rio Grande Valley: Subtropical South Texas

9.suitability_note_seasoned: Rio Grande Valley winters bank only about 0 to 300 chill hours, and a warm winter can come close to zero, per Texas A&M AgriLife Extension. fig.region_label: Rio Grande Valley: Subtropical South Texas

9.suitability_note_seasoned: Rio Grande Valley winters comfortably meet a fig's roughly 100-hour chill need, and the long, intensely hot growing season ripens a full crop, per Texas A&M AgriLife Extension fig production guidance and the Valley's near-zero-chill, essentially frost-free climate. Humid spells still bring fig rust and souring, so favor closed-eye, rust-tolerant varieties (Celeste, LSU Purple, Alma) and a well-drained, nematode-free site. Exact Valley bloom and harvest months are not separately published; this window is a conservative estimate carried over from the similarly warm, humid Gulf coast, where fig fruits reliably.
